anomalies.observed: The ATtiny45 U2 and ATtiny13 U3 are both present and their corresponding I/O and reset pins are connected to the same nets.
anomalies.expected: A fan controller should use one active MCU, or clearly designate these pin-compatible MCUs as mutually exclusive assembly alternatives. The files show no such exclusion; if both are populated, their I/O pins are electrically paralleled.

evidence.quote: PWM : J4.1(MISO,passive) R2.1(passive) R5.2(passive) U2.6(PB1,bidirectional) U3.6(PB1,bidirectional)
RST : J1.4(Pin_4,passive) J4.5(~{RST},passive) R3.2(passive) U2.1(~{RESET}/PB5,bidirectional) U3.1(~{RESET}/PB5,bidirectional)

anomalies.impact: If both MCUs are assembled, they can drive shared signal nets at the same time, causing output contention or conflicting control of the fan. If only one is intended, the build needs an explicit population exclusion or selection that is not shown here.

anomalies.observed: C2, the only capacitor shown across U1's +5V output and ground, is 100nF.
anomalies.expected: An LM1117-family regulator generally requires a substantially larger output capacitor for stable operation; a 100nF-only output capacitor is inadequate for the usual LM1117 stability requirement.
anomalies.impact: The +5V regulator output may oscillate or become unstable, potentially disrupting the MCU and other circuitry powered from +5V.

parsed.summary: The netlist connects two separate, pin-compatible ATtiny devices to the same control and I/O nets without indicating that they are mutually exclusive. The LM1117 output also has only a 100nF capacitor, which is generally insufficient for regulator stability.
